items.title: 这段关系值得继续吗？先看你有没有变得更清楚
items.hook: 值得继续的关系，会让你更像自己。
items.body: 如果你每天都在猜、等、证明，先暂停一下：关系不是考试，你也不是唯一的答题人。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; do not decide for the user

items.title: 不要为了不失去一个人，把自己缩小
items.hook: 爱不是让你一直降低需求。
items.body: 继续之前，先问：我是在选择这段关系，还是只是不敢面对失去？
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no pressure tactic

items.title: 真正的信号不是热闹，是能不能一起修复
items.hook: 有吸引不等于适合继续。
items.body: 看对方如何面对误会、边界和你的真实感受，比看一时的甜更重要。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no guaranteed interpretation

items.title: 如果你一直在单方面解释，对方可能没有在共同经营
items.hook: 关系需要两个人都愿意靠近事实。
items.body: 你可以表达一次，但不要把所有理解、安抚和修复都变成自己的任务。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no blame language

items.title: 继续不是忍耐，离开也不是失败
items.hook: 清楚地选择，比耗着更温柔。
items.body: 不急着下结论，先把模式、感受和现实放在同一张桌上看。
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no outcome guarantee

items.title: Is this worth continuing?
items.hook: If a relationship makes you smaller every day, pause before you call it love.
items.body: Scene 1: staring at an unanswered message. Scene 2: writing three versions of the same reply. Scene 3: ask whether this connection gives clarity or only anxiety.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no breakup instruction

items.title: Attraction is not enough
items.hook: Chemistry starts the story. Repair decides whether it can continue.
items.body: Use a calm voiceover: look for how both people handle misunderstandings, boundaries, and honest feelings.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no certainty claim

items.title: Fear of loss is not the same as commitment
items.hook: Sometimes you are not choosing them; you are avoiding the grief of change.
items.body: Prompt viewers to ask one honest question before acting: would I still choose this if I were not afraid?
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no diagnostic claim

items.title: One-sided explaining is data
items.hook: If you keep translating the relationship alone, that is information.
items.body: Show three text overlays: explaining, soothing, repairing. End with: a relationship needs shared reality.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no blame language

items.title: The calmer decision test
items.hook: Do not ask only whether they want you. Ask who you become here.
items.body: Use a quiet B-roll structure: notes, calendar, phone face-down, breath. End on a private reading CTA.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no outcome guarantee

items.title: Worth continuing test
items.hook: A relationship worth continuing should not require you to abandon yourself to keep it alive.
items.body: Before you chase certainty, ask whether the pattern is creating clarity, repair, and mutual effort.
items.notes: Manual publishing only

items.title: Fear versus choice
items.hook: Fear of losing someone can feel like love. It is not always the same thing.
items.body: A calmer question: would I still choose this connection if panic were not making the decision?
items.notes: Manual publishing only

items.title: Repair decides
items.hook: Attraction can be real and still not be enough.
items.body: Look at repair: how both people handle conflict, uncertainty, and honest needs.
items.notes: Manual publishing only

items.title: Shared reality
items.hook: If you are the only one explaining, soothing, and repairing, notice that.
items.body: One person can start a conversation. Two people have to build the reality.
items.cta: Get a calmer next step: https://tianji.love/ask
items.notes: Manual publishing only

items.title: Continuing is a choice
items.hook: Continuing is not the same as enduring.
items.body: The question is not only whether they stay. It is whether the relationship has room for your real self.
items.notes: Manual publishing only

items.title: How do I know if a relationship is worth continuing?
items.hook: Look less at intensity and more at repair.
items.body: A grounded way to evaluate it: does the relationship make room for honesty, boundaries, and mutual effort? Attraction matters, but repair is often the better signal. If you are the only person doing all the explaining and soothing, that is information. This is not a command to leave or stay; it is a prompt to look at the pattern calmly.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; disclose affiliation if posted

items.title: Am I staying because I love them or because I am afraid to lose them?
items.hook: Fear and love can feel similar when attachment is activated.
items.body: Try separating the question into two columns: what you genuinely value about the relationship, and what you are afraid will happen if it changes. If the second column is doing all the work, pause before making a big move.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no therapy/diagnosis framing

items.title: Is one-sided effort a sign to stop trying?
items.hook: One-sided effort does not prove the whole story, but it should not be ignored.
items.body: If you have already expressed your needs clearly and the relationship still depends on you translating, soothing, and repairing everything alone, that pattern deserves attention. The next step can be a calm boundary, not a dramatic ultimatum.
items.notes: Manual publishing only; no guaranteed outcome
